result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers reject the either/or framing and give concrete per-field behavior. Both also clear errors live once they appear, debounce the username check and use a hint for the password rule. A recommends validating on blur, so errors don't appear mid-typing and problems don't pile up at submit. B argues against blur and checks email only on submit, which misses the rubric's central recommendation, even though B adds useful extra details on accessibility and autofill. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): B recommends checking each field when the person leaves it, then re-checking live once an error shows. That is the balanced approach the rubric asks for. A rejects checking on leaving the field, defaults email to submit-only and leans toward the designer, so it misses item 2. Both handle the username debounce and password hint well and give concrete behavior for each field.
